content: Ross River virus disease is transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected mosquito. While the majority of individuals infected with the virus remain asymptomatic, those who do develop symptoms may experience joint pain and swelling, muscle pain, fever, fatigue, and a rash. Most patients recover within a few weeks; however, some may suffer from prolonged joint pain, joint stiffness, or fatigue lasting several months. Travelers to Australia and Papua New Guinea are at risk of contracting Ross River virus disease if bitten by an infected mosquito. This disease is the most prevalent mosquito-borne illness in Australia. Activities that increase the likelihood of infection include spending significant time outdoors and traveling during seasons when mosquito populations are higher, such as summer. Currently, there are no vaccines or medications available to prevent Ross River virus disease. Travelers can reduce their risk by taking the following precautions: 1. Use EPA-registered insect repellents containing active ingredients such as DEET, picaridin, IR3535, or oil of lemon eucalyptus (OLE). These repellents are safe and effective when used as directed, even for pregnant and breastfeeding women. If sunscreen is also being used, apply the insect repellent after the sunscreen. 2. For babies and children: Dress them in clothing that covers their arms and legs. Cover strollers and baby carriers with mosquito netting. When applying insect repellent: Follow the product label instructions carefully. Avoid using products containing OLE or para-menthane-diol (PMD) on children under 3 years old. Do not apply repellent to a child’s hands, eyes, mouth, cuts, or irritated skin. Adults should spray repellent onto their hands first and then apply it to the child’s face. If sunscreen is also used, apply the insect repellent after the sunscreen. 3. Treat clothing and gear (such as boots, pants, socks, and tents) with 0.5% permethrin or purchase pre-treated items. Permethrin is an insecticide that kills or repels mosquitoes and other insects. Permethrin-treated clothing remains protective after multiple washes; check the product label for details on the duration of protection. When treating items yourself, follow the product instructions carefully. Do not apply permethrin products directly to the skin. 4. Prevent mosquitoes from entering your accommodation: Choose lodging with air conditioning or window and door screens. If staying in a place without these features or sleeping outdoors, use a mosquito net. Select a compact, white, rectangular net with 156 holes per square inch that is long enough to tuck under the mattress. Permethrin-treated nets provide additional protection compared to untreated ones. Follow label instructions to determine if the net can be washed. 5. If bitten by mosquitoes, avoid scratching the bites. Apply over-the-counter anti-itch or antihistamine creams to alleviate itching. For more information, refer to resources on mosquito bite symptoms and treatment.
